system.name: DPA-Store
system.one_liner: an ordered network-data-path key-value store that maintains its index tree directly from the NIC

content.subject: how a NIC-triggered buffer patch merges into the host tree and propagates level by level to the root

elements.name: Inner
elements.role: an internal (non-leaf) node of the host tree; repeated at every internal position

elements.name: L
elements.role: a leaf node of the host tree holding data entries
an elided/collapsed subtree not relevant to this patch path

elements.name: NIC
elements.role: the network interface whose buffered insert triggered this patch

elements.name: buf
elements.role: the NIC's buffer holding entries not yet merged into the host tree

elements.name: Inner (new subtree)
elements.role: the newly trained subtree produced by merging buffered entries, not yet attached

elements.name: case A
elements.role: branch taken when step 2 produces exactly one new node

elements.name: case B
elements.role: branch taken when step 2 produces more than one new node, requiring the parent to be repeated

elements.name: lock icon (black)
elements.role: marks that a parent node is currently located and locked on the host

elements.name: lock icon (green)
elements.role: marks that a parent node has just been unlocked, releasing it

relations.what: the NIC's insert buffer fills up, triggering the patch thread
buffered entries are copied, merged, and trained into new leaf node(s)
the parent Inner node is located and locked on the host before it is modified
the parent's connection is updated to point at the top of the new subtree via enqueued copy-stitch and connect-stitch commands
the parent is unlocked once the new subtree is attached, letting old descendants detach for later reallocation

panels.label: i)
panels.differs: template: the rightmost Inner node at the lowest patched level has its parent locked (step 3) while its buffered NIC entry and a sibling leaf merge into one new leaf via steps 1-4, then the parent unlocks (step 5)

panels.label: ii)
panels.differs: the patch has propagated one level up: the previous new leaf now sits as a full Inner node (case A) or as two leaves (case B) attached under a newly locked parent one level higher

panels.label: iii)
panels.differs: the patch reaches the tree's root level: the new subtree (case A: one Inner node, or case B: two Inner nodes with leaf children) attaches under the root, which is locked then unlocked, and the process is marked 'patch finished'

steps.what: entries are copied, merged and trained into new node(s)
steps.carries: buffered entries turned into trained node(s)

steps.what: parent is located and locked on host
did step 2 result in exactly one new node? case A: yes, goto step 4; case B: no, repeat for parent at step 2
steps.carries: branch outcome (case A or case B)

steps.what: parent connection is updated with the top of the new subtree; copy-stitch and connect-stitch commands are enqueued
parent is unlocked; old descendants stay locked and are detached, with reallocation possible after the epoch period

content.key_idea: A five-step lock/copy/stitch/unlock protocol merges NIC-buffered entries into new tree nodes and, frame by frame, repeats itself one level higher up the host tree until the update reaches the root.
content.reading_order: Top to bottom through frames i)-iii); within each, follow the red NIC arrow and circled steps 1-5 from the buffer up into the locked parent.

pale-pink fill of the 'buf' circle icon
gold/orange fill and outline of the newly trained subtree nodes (Inner/L) being attached

style.fill: flat, with the new subtree filled solid gold/orange against otherwise unfilled white tree boxes
style.stroke: thin black tree-box outlines; thin orange/gold lines connecting the buffer to the new subtree; dashed grey outlines on the case A/B labels

encoding.color_means: red marks the NIC and its buffered insert path; gold/orange marks the newly trained subtree not yet fully attached; black vs green padlocks mark a parent node as locked vs just unlocked; grey dashed labels mark the two branches, case A and case B
encoding.line_style_means: solid black lines draw the fixed tree structure; curved gold lines trace how buffered/leaf data feeds into the new subtree; dashed grey brackets group the case A and case B alternatives
encoding.state_means: the three frames (i, ii, iii) are told apart by which tree level currently holds the locked parent and the gold new-subtree, showing the patch has moved up one level each time
encoding.marker_means: circled numbers 1-5 and a circled '?' order the steps of the protocol listed at the right, repeated identically inside each of the three frames
encoding.emphasis: the gold-highlighted new subtree and the black/green padlock pair draw the eye to exactly which node is being modified and whether it is currently locked, in every frame
reusable_patterns: an identical numbered lock/copy/stitch/unlock recipe replayed at successively higher tree levels across three stacked frames, with a shared side legend spelling out each numbered step
weaknesses: case A and case B are only distinguished by a small grey dashed tag, easy to miss next to the much bolder gold highlighting
the same step numbers (1-5) repeat in every frame without a frame-level index, so referring to 'step 3' alone does not say which frame

evidence: we propagate the changes to the NIC-side tree using our stitcher threads
We enqueue the individual node updates to the stitcher queues as COPY stitches
a single CONNECT stitch command is issued that translates to a single pointer swap

summary: Figure 6 walks through DPA-Store's host-side patching protocol as it climbs the host tree one level per frame (i, ii, iii). In each frame, the same numbered recipe applies: a 'Patch' thread reacts to an insert-buffer-full command from the NIC (1), buffered entries are copied, merged, and trained into new node(s) (2), the parent is located and locked on the host (3), and a branch decides whether step 2 produced exactly one new node (case A, proceed) or more than one (case B, repeat at the parent). Once resolved, the parent's connection is updated to point at the new gold-highlighted subtree via enqueued copy-stitch and connect-stitch commands (4), and the parent is unlocked while its old, now-detached descendants remain reallocatable after an epoch (5). Frame iii reaches the root and the patch is marked finished.
summary_zh: 图6展示DPA-Store主机补丁协议逐层更新宿主树：每帧重复同一编号步骤——收到缓冲区满命令、条目合并成新节点、锁定父节点、按case A/B分支更新父连接并解锁，直到根节点补丁完成。
notes: corrected primary group from the prior 'walkthrough' to 'evolution' (walkthrough kept as a secondary label): the figure redraws the same host-tree instance in three stacked frames (i, ii, iii) as the patch climbs one level per frame, which the v3 rule ranks as evolution before walkthrough; the numbered 1-5 protocol is a step recipe repeated identically inside each frame rather than one continuous path.
